newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sends troops for possible Zaire rescue.
newsitem.headline: France sends troops for possible Zaire rescue.

text.p: In a sign of growing concern about the crisis in Zaire, France said on Thursday it had sent aircraft and about 100 troops to Congo and Gabon in case it has to protect or evacuate its nationals from the war-torn country.

"Given the situation, and in order to ensure the safety of our citizens if necessary, the Ministry of Defence has decided to send extra resources to Libreville and Brazzaville," Defence Ministry spokesman Pierre Servent told a briefing.
Rebels based in eastern Zaire have captured more than one fifth of the sprawling country, including its third-biggest city, Kisangani, sparking fears of violence, looting or a coup in Kinshasa.

The measures, which Servent called a precaution, were announced a day after France expressed growing concern about events in Zaire and said it was taking steps to protect an estimated 1,300 French citizens in the central African state.
Defence ministry officials said three transport planes -- two C160 Transals and a C130 Hercules -- and two Puma helicopters had been sent to the Gabonese capital Libreville with 40 extra soldiers.
They are in addition to the 600 troops France regularly keeps based in oil-producing Gabon.
The other 60 soldiers will go on to the Congolese capital Brazzaville, across the Zaire river from Kinshasa, they said.
France put in place a similar deployment last November, but withdrew it discreetly in December when the initial panic caused by the rebels' first victories in eastern Zaire calmed down.
France sent troops to Kinshasa to protect and evacuate foreign nationals in 1991 and 1993 when unpaid army soldiers rampaged through the capital and other cities.
